name: quota-ladder-sol61-v11.1-quality
description: Every exact head is triaged by gpt-6.1-sol (low effort) into trivial/low/normal/critical (normal is the default; critical requires both a large/intricate diff and a critical surface); the tier sets the reviewer --effort per phase. Phase 1 runs the general reviewer plus rust-quality (when selected) only, on a quota ladder: gemini-3.8-flash-high while the Antigravity Gemini quota lasts, else glm-5.3-flash while the Z.AI plan lasts and the tier asks at most high effort, else muse-spark-1.3-contributor; validated by a fresh distinct gpt-6.1-sol gate verifier (effort medium). The gate scores the verified Phase-1 findings (blocking 3, suggestion 1, nitpick 0) and defers Phase 2 only above 5 points; otherwise Phase-2 gpt-6.1-sol reviewers (general and every selected specialist) run at the tier's phase2 effort and a fresh distinct gpt-6.1-sol final verifier (fixed high) weighs both phases. A trivial tier publishes the final review from Phase 1 alone unless a verified blocker keeps it preliminary. The critical tier is single stage: no gate, the Phase-1 reviewers run beside the Phase-2 reviewers and the final verifier weighs both; a failed Phase 1 is dropped and disclosed. dash-evo-tool, yappr and grovedb have no Phase 1 (straight to Phase 2; trivial at low). Model comparison: on 25% of critical runs every Phase-2 reviewer also runs on gpt-6-astra; the gpt-6.1-sol verifier weighs both sets blind. Degraded mode: while the OpenAI/Codex pool answers with quota errors every gpt-* lane runs on muse-spark-1.3-contributor, no comparison runs, Phase 1 is capped at high effort, the review is titled DEGRADED and never approves. v11.1 (2026-10-16): same lanes and models; prompts gain the 'introduced or by its nature responsible' scope test, premise/sibling/sequence/base checks, considered_dismissed, tracked-deferral rule and CI-as-evidence rule; Platform/GroveDB gain non-consensus and layer-ownership blocking classes; tenderdash-consensus-security is offered on dashpay/platform ABCI changes.

triage.label: complexity-triage

trivial.meaning: typo/docs/rename/format/config-only, no behaviour change; Phase 2 skipped

normal.meaning: the default: an ordinary change to logic, tests, tooling, UI or build, including large or cross-cutting ones, unless it meets the bar for critical

critical.meaning: BOTH large/intricate AND the diff changes a critical surface (consensus, funds/coin selection, crypto, signatures/keys, peer-facing deserialization, migrations); size alone never qualifies; never above xhigh; single stage: the author is expected to have reviewed it closely, so Phase 1 runs beside Phase 2 with no gate

triage.rule: normal is the default; critical only when both large/intricate and on a critical surface, naming the file/function; when unsure pick the lower tier. effort per phase = tiers[tier]; verifiers keep their fixed reasoning; Phase-1 findings above the gate budget publish preliminary regardless of tier, except on the single-stage critical tier, which has no gate

reviewer.label: phase1-quota-ladder
reviewer.effort_note: default; the triage tier overrides --effort per run and the value used is persisted per lane. `candidates` below is the ordered Phase-1 ladder; this block is the shared default for agent/launch.

candidates.label: phase1-gemini-flash
candidates.note: included Antigravity subscription; gated on the Gemini group's 5h and weekly buckets

candidates.label: phase1-glm-flash
candidates.note: Z.AI coding plan; gated on its 5h and weekly credit windows. Fine up to `high`, but at `max` it thinks for 50-150 min per lane (measured 2026-09-09..16: median 51, p90 136), so tiers asking `max` pass over it

candidates.label: phase1-muse-contrib
candidates.note: pay-per-token last rung (Meta contributor tier, ~$0.10/$0.20 per M; no `max` effort on this tier); never gated

phase1.ladder_rule: Phase 1 runs on the first candidate whose subscription has at least quota_reserve of every window left and whose use_up_to ceiling (if any) is at or above the tier's phase1 effort; a failed lookup skips the rung; the last rung is never gated. The chosen model is disclosed in the provenance block and persisted per lane.
phase1.specialists_note: Phase 1 runs general plus only these specialists (when selected); Phase 2 runs every selected specialist. 2026-09-30 audit: the other Phase-1 specialists produced ~0 unique fixed findings per token.

gate.rule: Phase 2 is deferred only when the verified Phase-1 findings score above block_above; under it, Phase 2 runs and the final verifier re-adjudicates the Phase-1 findings. A preliminary review held back by suggestions alone never approves.

reviewer.label: phase2-sol
reviewer.effort_note: default; the triage tier overrides --effort per run and the value used is persisted per lane

preliminary.title: Preliminary review — Phase 1 blocker gate
preliminary.phase2: Phase 2 (gpt-6.1-sol) not run (deferred by blocker gate)

final_phase1_only.title: Final review — Phase 1 only ({tier} change)
final_phase1_only.phase2: not run (triage rated this change trivial)
final_phase1_only.event: COMMENT (never APPROVE: Phase 2 did not run)

checkpoint_migration: same-head policy identity or fingerprint mismatch restarts Phase 1; mismatched evidence cannot resume or satisfy policy v3
provenance_rule: Persist exact policy identity/fingerprint, head, phase, decision, canonical blocker count, reviewer/verifier attempt IDs, logical agents, exact backend models, per-lane --effort and the triage tier/model/reasoning, harness/auth/roles/read-only launch contract, PIDs, exit statuses, artifacts, status/parseability, prior-finding revalidation, deterministic policy result, coverage, publication IDs, and every verifier attempt.

degraded.label: degraded

gpt-6.1-sol.note: Meta contributor tier has no `max`; xhigh is its top

gpt-6-astra.note: Meta contributor tier has no `max`; xhigh is its top

degraded.rule: Active while the sentinel answers a quota error (429 / cooling down / usage limit) or an operator ran `reviewsys degraded on`. Phase 1 keeps its ladder (gemini-3.8-flash-high -> glm-5.3-flash -> muse) with the tier effort capped at `phase1_effort_cap`; every other lane whose model is listed in `substitutes` runs on its stand-in at min(lane effort, effort_cap). Both phases run, except when more heads than `backlog_skip_phase1_above` are queued: backlog mode still applies in degraded mode (`backlog_skip_phase1`), so a deep queue goes straight to Phase 2 on the stand-in rather than waiting on the slow Phase-1 rungs. APPROVE is downgraded to COMMENT; every publication carries the DEGRADED badge and the reason. No model comparison runs while degraded. Clears automatically when the sentinel answers again.

comparison.label: sol61-vs-astra
comparison.rule: On a sampled run every Phase-2 reviewer lane (general and each specialist, fresh final pass included) also runs on `model` at the same effort; the verifier sees both sets without model names and alone decides the verdict. Never in degraded mode or on audits. Compare with `reviewsys compare`.
